{{short description|Propositions that are demonstrably, necessarily or self-evidently true}}
"'''Apodictic'''", also spelled "'''apodeictic'''" ({{langx|grc|ἀποδεικτικός}}, "capable of demonstration"), is an [[adjective|adjectival]] expression from [[syllogism|Aristotelian logic]] that refers to [[proposition]]s that are demonstrably, necessarily or [[self-evident]]ly true.<ref>[http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/apodictic Dictionary definitions of apodictic], from dictionary.com, including material from the [[Random House Unabridged Dictionary]], [[Random House|Random House, Inc.]] (2006), [[The American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language]], Fourth Edition, 2006 by [[Houghton Mifflin Company]], and [[WordNet]] 3.0, [[Princeton University]] 2006.</ref> '''Apodicticity''' or [[wikt:apodixis|apodixis]] is the corresponding [[abstract noun]], referring to [[logical truth|logical certainty]].

Apodictic propositions contrast with [[assertoric]] propositions, which merely assert that something is (or is not) true, and with problematic propositions, which assert only the possibility of something's being true. Apodictic judgments are clearly provable or logically certain. For instance, "Three plus one equals four" is apodictic, because it is true by definition. "Chicago is larger than Omaha" is assertoric. "A corporation could be wealthier than a country" is problematic. In [[Aristotelianism|Aristotelian]] logic, "apodictic" is opposed to "[[dialectic]]", as [[scientific proof]] is opposed to philosophical [[reasoning]]. [[Immanuel Kant|Kant]] contrasted "apodictic" with "problematic" and "assertoric" in the ''[[Critique of Pure Reason]]'' (A70/B95 - A76/B101).<ref name="EB1911">{{Cite EB1911|wstitle=Apodictic|volume=2|page=183}}</ref>

==Apodictic a priorism==
[[Hans Reichenbach]], one of the founders of [[logical positivism]], offered a modified version of [[Immanuel Kant]]'s [[a priorism]] by distinguishing between ''apodictic a priorism'' and ''constitutive a priorism''.<ref name="Mormann">{{cite book|last1=Mormann|first1=Thomas|authorlink1=Thomas Mormann |chapter=Toward a Theory of the Pragmatic a Priori: From Carnap to Lewis and Beyond |title=Rudolf Carnap and the Legacy of Logical Empiricism |series=[[Institute Vienna Circle / Vienna Circle Society#Activities|Vienna Circle Institute Yearbook]]|date=2012|volume=16 |publisher=Springer Science+Business Media|location=Dordrecht|editor-last1=Creath|editor-first=Richard|editor-link1=Richard Creath |isbn=978-94-007-3928-4|pages=[https://books.google.com/books?id=ICZCs7BfxboC&pg=PT112&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q&f=false 113-132]|edition=2012.|doi=10.1007/978-94-007-3929-1_7|s2cid=170999667 |chapter-url=https://philpapers.org/rec/MORTAT-4 }}</ref>
